microtheory.name: acoustics
microtheory.definition: Physics of sound — wave equation, propagation, reflection, diffraction, absorption, room behavior, source characteristics. The mechanical foundation underlying everything the substrate's audio pipeline processes. Substrate analogue: the input characteristics the cochlear gammatone filterbank receives.

concepts.name: wave_equation
concepts.definition: ∂²p/∂t² = c² ∇²p. Governs how pressure waves propagate. Substrate analogue: physical model behind substrate's audio input.

concepts.name: speed_of_sound
concepts.definition: c ≈ 343 m/s in dry air at 20°C. Increases with temperature + humidity. Substrate analogue: implicit constant in substrate's wavelength-frequency relation.

concepts.name: sound_pressure_level
concepts.definition: SPL in dB SPL = 20 log10(p/p_ref) where p_ref = 20 μPa. Hearing threshold ~0 dB SPL; pain threshold ~120 dB. Substrate analogue: substrate's input gain calibration.

concepts.name: intensity
concepts.definition: Power per unit area, W/m². Proportional to p²/(ρc). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-channel power calculation.

concepts.name: inverse_square_law
concepts.definition: Free-field intensity falls 6 dB per doubling of distance. Substrate analogue: substrate's distance-from-source modeling.

concepts.name: reflection
concepts.definition: Sound bouncing off surface. Specular (smooth) or diffuse (rough). Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-arrival signal detection.

concepts.name: absorption
concepts.definition: Sound energy converting to heat in materials. Frequency-dependent — high frequencies absorbed more. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-dependent envelope decay.

concepts.name: diffraction
concepts.definition: Sound bending around obstacles when wavelength is comparable to obstacle size. Low frequencies diffract more. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-localization with occluders.

concepts.name: refraction
concepts.definition: Sound bending due to medium variation — temperature gradients, wind. Substrate analogue: substrate's anomalous-path detection.

concepts.name: interference
concepts.definition: Constructive + destructive superposition of waves. Standing waves in rooms. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial pattern from interfering sources.

concepts.name: resonance
concepts.definition: Frequency at which a system naturally vibrates. String, air column, room mode. Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone channel center frequencies.

concepts.name: natural_frequency
concepts.definition: Frequency of unforced oscillation, determined by mass + stiffness. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin attractor frequencies.

concepts.name: damping
concepts.definition: Energy dissipation reducing oscillation amplitude over time. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ decay rate.

concepts.name: Q_factor
concepts.definition: Quality factor. Bandwidth at half-power normalized to center frequency. High Q = narrow + ringy; low Q = wide + damped. Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone filter Q.

concepts.name: mode
concepts.definition: Spatial pattern of natural vibration. Strings have nodes + antinodes; rooms have standing waves at specific places. Substrate analogue: substrate's room-mode detector.

concepts.name: room_acoustics
concepts.definition: How rooms shape sound — reverberation, modes, early reflections, diffusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-vs-environment separation.

concepts.name: reverberation_time
concepts.definition: RT60 — time for sound to decay 60 dB after source stops. Sabine's equation. Substrate analogue: substrate's decay-envelope time-constant.

concepts.name: early_reflections
concepts.definition: Reflections arriving within ~80ms of direct sound. Crucial for spaciousness perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-image clustering.

concepts.name: diffuse_field
concepts.definition: Late reverb where reflections are too dense to distinguish. Substrate analogue: substrate's noise-background estimation.

concepts.name: haas_effect
concepts.definition: Two sounds within ~30ms are fused; later one is heard as direction-coloring. Helmut Haas 1949. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-fusion temporal window.

concepts.name: sound_source
concepts.definition: Origin of acoustic energy. Point, line, volume sources. Substrate analogue: substrate's signal-origin localizer.

concepts.name: directivity_pattern
concepts.definition: How a source radiates in different directions. Omnidirectional, cardioid, figure-8. Substrate analogue: substrate's source-orientation tracker.

concepts.name: near_field_far_field
concepts.definition: Near sources: pressure + velocity in phase; far: in quadrature. Different localization cues. Substrate analogue: substrate's distance estimation.

concepts.name: doppler_effect
concepts.definition: Frequency shift due to relative motion. Substrate analogue: substrate's velocity-from-frequency-shift detector.

rules.name: wave_equation_governs_propagation
rules.head: sound propagates through any medium
rules.body: the wave equation determines pressure at every point + time. Substrate's audio input has wave-equation history.

rules.name: high_frequencies_absorb_faster
rules.head: sound travels distance through air
rules.body: high frequencies attenuate more than low. Substrate's distance-correction in source-direction estimation should account for this.

rules.name: low_frequencies_diffract_around_obstacles
rules.head: sound encounters an obstacle of size comparable to wavelength
rules.body: low frequencies diffract; high frequencies cast acoustic shadow. Substrate's occlusion handling.

rules.name: reverberation_blurs_temporal_detail
rules.head: the substrate processes sound in a reverberant room
rules.body: early reflections + late reverb mask onset transients. Substrate's source-vs-reverb separation needs to address this.

rules.name: haas_effect_fuses_close_arrivals
rules.head: two arrivals of similar amplitude within 30ms
rules.body: the substrate perceives them as one source localized to the first; later arrivals color but don't separate. Substrate's source-fusion threshold.
